These merchants prey upon the adult’s regret, offering a fleeting solace in the illusion of recaptured youth. Yet, the very act of seeking such artificial comfort betrays the depth of the loss. For true innocence, once departed, cannot be purchased or recreated, only mourned – a phantom limb aching with the memory of what once was, and can never be again.
